question: Which benchmark and metric split best isolates transfer to deeper hops (e.g. accuracy as a function of hop depth on 2WikiMultiHopQA / MoreHopQA / HotpotQA-style sets)?
description: The claim of transfer to deeper multi-hop queries needs a hop-depth-stratified evaluation. Retrieved benchmarks 2WikiMultiHopQA (arxiv:2011.01060) and MoreHopQA (arxiv:2406.13397) explicitly address comprehensive reasoning-step evaluation, but the exact stratification and the metric (EM vs F1 vs faithfulness) still need to be fixed.
confidence_basis: Based on reading two full-text benchmark/hop-annotation sources and one full-text hop-stratified model paper; the specific stratification and power still need to be fixed in the experiment plan.
rationale: Without hop-depth stratification the central 'deeper transfer' claim is untestable and could be an artifact of aggregate accuracy.
resolution: Reading resolves the design direction, not the exact metric. arxiv:2101.03737 supplies hop-stratified splits with per-depth numbers (MetaQA-1/2/3-hop with Hits@1 and F1) and shows 1-2 hop is near-saturated, so the transfer claim must be evaluated on 3+ hop strata and on unsaturised WebQSP/CWQ. arxiv:2011.01060 supplies gold evidence paths that let one distinguish chain triples from context triples and measure evidence faithfulness. arxiv:2406.13397 supplies a sub-question 'perfect reasoning' rate that is a ready operationalization for detecting one-hop failures. The remaining choice — primary metric per stratum and the power achievable on 3+ hop test sets — belongs to the experiment plan.
